summary: The Legion daemon wakes an open production check once per successful Apply job of a configured deploy workflow's run on the default branch whose step finished after the pull request's GitHub merged_at. legion.yaml gains projects.<KEY>.deploys [{repo, workflow, step}]; Envoy's workflow_run 'completed' envelope becomes intake.WorkflowRunCompleted; the engine queues a check_compare row carrying a deploy object (no new outbox kind, no migration) per open check of that repository; the executor reads, as the implement App, the pull request (merged_at), the run attempt (path, head_branch, head_repository, event) and its jobs (steps), and applies intake.CheckWake cause 'deploy run' under event id check-wake:<issue>:<checkID>:deploy run:<run>:<attempt>:<job id>. The existing wake rule (one pending cause while a look is open) is unchanged.

decisions.detail: projects.<KEY>.deploys: list of {repo: owner/name, workflow: .github/workflows/<file>.y(a)ml, step: non-empty}; duplicate repo+workflow refused; mirrored in api settings (no daemon API version bump, api/version.go:292-296).
workflow is the run's top-level file (workflow_run.path); a workflow_call caller is a different run and is matched only when configured.
Envoy's workflow_run completed envelope (notifications.github.<o>.<r>.workflow.<file>.completed), whatever the run's conclusion.

A job of that attempt (run_attempt equal) whose step named `step` concluded success with completed_at strictly after the pull request's merged_at; both GitHub timestamps; no tree comparison and no applied-commit annotation read.

The executor re-reads the run attempt: path equals the configured workflow, head_branch equals the issue's recorded default branch, head_repository equals the check's repository, event is neither pull_request nor pull_request_target; 404 wakes nothing; other failures retry.

One CheckWake per check and Apply job (event id includes run, attempt and job id); the same run delivered twice adds no look; two Apply jobs give two wakes, the second kept for the next look; a re-run attempt has new job ids and wakes again.
Existing rule unchanged: while a look is open or the issue runs again, the first cause is kept and later ones ignored; the next look starts after every ignored deploy completed, so none goes unseen.

record.CheckCompare gains Deploy *DeployRun (exactly one of Build and Deploy); avoids a new outbox kind because open PRs #2188, #2173, #2163, #2150, #2131 each add migration 0051 and several rewrite outbox_kind_check.
'deploy run'; detail '<repo> <workflow> run <id> attempt <n>, job <job name>: <step> succeeded at <RFC 3339>'; task wording 'the deploy workflow's run: <detail>'.

findings.finding: The wake unit (per Apply, per run, per attempt) and the trigger timing were unresolved.
findings.answer: Decision 6: one wake per successful Apply job (event id includes the job id), so two applies give two looks in one run or two; the same run delivered twice adds none; a re-run attempt has new jobs and wakes again. Decision 3: triggered at the attempt's workflow_run completed, recorded as spec departure 1.

findings.finding: The one pending-cause slot means later deploys during an open look are ignored, and their fact ids are recorded as processed.
findings.answer: Decision 7: kept unchanged and lossless — the next look starts only after every ignored deploy completed, so it sees them; spec A4 asks exactly that an apply during a look is kept for the next look. Tests 4 and 7d cover deploy behind build/issue.deployed and the reverse.

findings.finding: The draft compared the Apply time with the check's OpenedAt (daemon clock) instead of the merge time.
findings.answer: Decision 4: step completed_at strictly after the pull request's merged_at, both GitHub timestamps read in the same row (GET /pulls/{n}); equal times wake nothing (task 6 test).

findings.finding: Falling back to run.head_sha when the applied-commit annotation is missing is not supported by agent-infra's workflow.
findings.answer: Dropped: no tree comparison and no annotation read (decision 4). The look itself reads applied-commit per agent-infra's instructions.

findings.finding: The merge-containment guard was an extra condition the root's per-Apply promise does not state.
findings.answer: Dropped: any successful Apply after merged_at wakes, whichever run, as the root says (decision 4).

findings.finding: The new legion.yaml key needs a rollout order, since older daemons refuse unknown project keys.
findings.answer: Named for the root in plan.md 'For the root' and forRoot.ordering: the value lands with or after INFRA's image moves to the first release carrying this change, validated with that release's --check-config.

findings.finding: Annotations are addressed by check-run id, not job id, and are paginated.
findings.answer: Moot: the plan reads no annotations.

findings.finding: 'workflow' is ambiguous for reusable workflows reached through workflow_call.
findings.answer: Decision 2: the run's top-level file (workflow_run.path); a caller is matched only when configured; agent-infra's deploys are top-level envoy.yaml runs. Rig test 7f covers a run of another file.

findings.finding: Per-check reads (run, jobs, annotations) multiply cost and may exceed the 30 s row timeout.
findings.answer: Decision 10: three core reads per open check per completed run (pull request, run attempt, jobs; jobs read across pages), no annotations; same budgets and timeout as check_compare; task 6 tests two job pages.

findings.finding: Acceptance must exercise the real GitHub intake boundary with a source=github workflow envelope, not a direct fact or the Dispatch-sourced publish helper.
findings.answer: Task 3 pins the envelope with Envoy's own normalizer golden; task 7 publishes source=github envelopes through the durable consumer; task 11 does the same against real GitHub reads.

specDepartures.spec: Root spec 'Legion's deploy wake': the daemon wakes the check each time an Apply step of an envoy.yaml run on main succeeds after the merge.
specDepartures.plan: Each successful Apply job's wake is applied when its run attempt's workflow_run completed webhook arrives, not when the step itself finishes (decision 3).
specDepartures.evidence: One workflow_run webhook per attempt carries the workflow path the engine filters on (packages/envoy/internal/contracts/normalize.go:833-852); Envoy's job envelope carries no path (normalize.go:853-870) and would need a GitHub read for every default-branch job; agent-infra's check instructions read a run once it has a conclusion (legion/instructions/infra.md on agent-infra#151, lines 216-224).

risks: Envoy drops a workflow_run whose pull_requests list is non-empty (normalize.go:42-44); a squash merge's push run on main carries none (measured 0 on sjawhar/legion run 40203304600).
A rollback to a daemon older than this change fails a pending check_compare row carrying deploy under its strict decoder until the row is removed.
